this is f*cking gold.

Google engineers and MIT researchers ran 260 controlled agent experiments across 6 benchmarks, 5 architectures, and the OpenAI, Gemini, and Claude model families to find out when Multi Agent systems actually help and when adding more agents quietly destroys performance

best case: +80.8% 
worst case: −70.0%

below it, extra agents can help. 
above it, coordination often becomes pure overhead.

error amplification also hit 17.2× in independent parallel systems.  
their final framework predicts the right architecture with 87% accuracy.

hits.name: wast3
hits.text:
Anthropic engineer open sourced the memory layer he runs behind every agent he ships - and it makes vector search look like a toy

41 memory types, 9 write gates, 6 decay curves, MIT license

MEMENTO replaces "stuff the last 50 messages into the prompt" with something that decides what deserves to survive

nothing is remembered because it happened. every fact has to earn a slot, and every slot has an expiry attached to it

• how a fact gets in

> intake - a claim is split from its source, so the fact and who said it never fuse into one blob
> gate - nine checks before a write, including whether the fact already exists in another wording
> conflict - a new fact that contradicts an old one does not overwrite it. both stay, with a timestamp
> scope - facts about a person, a project and a preference go to separate stores, never one pile
> decay - anything unread for long enough loses weight until retrieval stops finding it

the conflict rule is the piece almost nobody builds

every memory system on the market silently overwrites. yours has been quietly wrong for months and you cannot tell, because the old version is gone

this one keeps the trail, so you can see the exact turn a fact changed and what caused it

• what comes back out

> recall - retrieval walks relations, so you get the three facts that connect instead of ten that merely match
> summary - compaction rewrites the context to the same meaning at a fraction of the tokens
> proof - every answer names the memories it used, by id
> forget - a real delete, including anything that was derived from the deleted fact
> replay - rebuild the agent's belief state as it stood on any past date

clone it, cut it to your own domain, and run it behind one agent by tomorrow

start with intake and the gate only
turning on all 41 memory types before you have traffic is the fastest way to build a slower vector store

the developers who wire this in stop re-explaining themselves to their own agents, permanently
hits.hook: An Anthropic engineer open-sourced MEMENTO — 41 memory types, 9 write gates, 6 decay curves — and it makes vector search look like a toy because nothing is remembered just because it happened.
hits.draft_en:
Anthropic engineer open sourced the memory layer he runs behind every agent he ships — and it makes vector search look like a toy.

41 memory types. 9 write gates. 6 decay curves. MIT license.

MEMENTO replaces "stuff the last 50 messages into the prompt" with something that decides what deserves to survive.

Nothing is remembered because it happened. Every fact has to earn a slot, and every slot has an expiry attached to it.

How a fact gets in:
> intake — claim split from its source, so the fact and who said it never fuse
> gate — nine checks before a write, including whether the fact already exists in another wording
> conflict — a new fact that contradicts an old one does not overwrite it. Both stay, with a timestamp
> scope — person, project, and preference go to separate stores
> decay — anything unread long enough loses weight until retrieval stops finding it

The conflict rule is the piece almost nobody builds. Every memory system on the market silently overwrites. Yours has been quietly wrong for months and you cannot tell, because the old version is gone.

What comes back out: recall that walks relations, summary that keeps meaning at a fraction of the tokens, proof by memory id, a real forget including derived facts, and replay of the agent's belief state on any past date.

Clone it. Cut it to your domain. Start with intake and the gate only — turning on all 41 memory types before you have traffic is the fastest way to build a slower vector store.

The developers who wire this in stop re-explaining themselves to their own agents, permanently.

virals.name: h100envy
virals.text:
I BUILT 6 AI AGENTS THAT SNIPE MEMECOINS ON ROBINHOOD CHAIN AND THE REFLEX THAT COSTS $0.00 SAVED ME MORE THAN THE MODEL THAT COSTS $0.008

$500 in. 3 nights. $4,370 out. i mass checked nothing manually.

> Scanner watches every new pool launch 24/7. pure code, no LLM, never sleeps
> Analyst gets metrics only. no addresses, no keys, no tx. returns pass or reject
> Risk runs 7 reflexes before the model is even called. kill switch, daily loss, gas cap, liquidity floor, slippage ceiling, duplicate check, max positions
> Executor only fires if every node above said yes. one rejection anywhere and the impulse dies
> Monitor watches every open position and drags stops
> Reporter sends the morning brief with the full funnel

night one: scanner caught 140 pools. reflexes killed 91 before the analyst saw them. analyst rejected 43. risk cut 4 more. 2 went through.

97% of memecoins die in 24 hours. the spine dropped 98.6% of them before a single dollar moved.

the reflex i almost removed is low_liquidity. felt too aggressive at $50K floor. then friday a pool passed the analyst at 89 confidence, mint renounced, lp locked, everything clean.

reflex caught it at $38K liquidity. i checked manually. rug pulled 40 minutes later.

a $0.00 check saved me from a pool that a $0.008 model approved.

every decision lives in sqlite. open any impulse from last week:

scanner:pending → analyst:pass → risk:reject(daily loss limit)

not something broke. exactly who, when, and why.

the model influences the score through confidence but cannot flip it. a pool with active mint will not score high no matter what gpt-6 astra says. the math has veto power over the brain.

want a 7th agent? one line. spine.add_node(). the other six do not know it exists and require zero changes.

the full protocol, all six nodes, every reflex, and the audit trail are in the article below

if a zero cost reflex outperforms a paid model call, what does that say about where safety actually lives?

outsiders.name: h100envy
outsiders.text:
I BUILT 6 AI AGENTS THAT SNIPE MEMECOINS ON ROBINHOOD CHAIN AND THE REFLEX THAT COSTS $0.00 SAVED ME MORE THAN THE MODEL THAT COSTS $0.008

$500 in. 3 nights. $4,370 out. i mass checked nothing manually.

> Scanner watches every new pool launch 24/7. pure code, no LLM, never sleeps
> Analyst gets metrics only. no addresses, no keys, no tx. returns pass or reject
> Risk runs 7 reflexes before the model is even called. kill switch, daily loss, gas cap, liquidity floor, slippage ceiling, duplicate check, max positions
> Executor only fires if every node above said yes. one rejection anywhere and the impulse dies
> Monitor watches every open position and drags stops
> Reporter sends the morning brief with the full funnel

night one: scanner caught 140 pools. reflexes killed 91 before the analyst saw them. analyst rejected 43. risk cut 4 more. 2 went through.

97% of memecoins die in 24 hours. the spine dropped 98.6% of them before a single dollar moved.

the reflex i almost removed is low_liquidity. felt too aggressive at $50K floor. then friday a pool passed the analyst at 89 confidence, mint renounced, lp locked, everything clean.

reflex caught it at $38K liquidity. i checked manually. rug pulled 40 minutes later.

a $0.00 check saved me from a pool that a $0.008 model approved.

every decision lives in sqlite. open any impulse from last week:

scanner:pending → analyst:pass → risk:reject(daily loss limit)

not something broke. exactly who, when, and why.

the model influences the score through confidence but cannot flip it. a pool with active mint will not score high no matter what gpt-6 astra says. the math has veto power over the brain.

want a 7th agent? one line. spine.add_node(). the other six do not know it exists and require zero changes.

the full protocol, all six nodes, every reflex, and the audit trail are in the article below

if a zero cost reflex outperforms a paid model call, what does that say about where safety actually lives?
outsiders.video_tip: 20–30s agent spine HUD: Scanner→Analyst→Risk→Executor funnel → 98.6% killed → $0 reflex saves vs $0.008 model.
outsiders.hook: Six memecoin-sniping agents on Robinhood Chain: a $0 liquidity reflex beat a $0.008 model call and saved a rug.
